title: Senior's toolkit: classes, errors, lint and tests
summary: Private state that is really private, errors that keep their cause, and the lint and test commands every TypeScript repository runs.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: classes, errors, lint and tests
steps.body: Classes and error types are where a codebase's rules live, and lint plus tests are what keep those rules from breaking. These are the language features and commands you will meet in any serious TypeScript repository.

toolkit.what: A JavaScript private field: really private at run time. TypeScript's `private` keyword is only checked by the compiler and disappears from the output.
flags: enforced by the engine; not in `Object.keys` or `JSON.stringify`
compile-time only; still readable as `obj.field` from plain JS
parameter properties are not supported when Node strips types

toolkit.what: Wrap a low-level error in one that says what you were doing, without losing the original. Node prints the `[cause]` chain in the stack trace.
flags: read it back when logging or handling
toolkit.example:
try { await db.query(sql); }
catch (err) { throw new Error(`Could not load order ${id}`, { cause: err }); }

toolkit.what: A custom error type, so callers can branch with `instanceof` instead of comparing message strings.
flags: shows in logs and stack traces instead of plain `Error`
the check to map it to a 404

toolkit.what: Lint the project and fix what can be fixed automatically. ESLint 9 reads `eslint.config.js` (the flat config); typescript-eslint adds the TypeScript rules.
flags: fail when there is any warning (CI)

toolkit.what: The lint rule that flags a promise nobody awaits or handles: the cause of silently lost errors. It needs typed linting (`parserOptions.projectService: true`).
flags: fail lint on an unhandled promise
its partner: an async function passed where a void callback is expected

toolkit.what: Run the tests. In a terminal it starts in watch mode and reruns only the tests affected by each save; in CI it runs once.
flags: run once and exit (what CI does)
only this file (any path fragment works)
report which lines the tests ran

toolkit.what: Check formatting. Teams let Prettier decide formatting so reviews never argue about it.

steps.prompt: Some orders are never saved, and there is no error in the logs. The handler contains `saveOrder(order);` and then `res.status(201).end();`. `saveOrder` is async. What catches this class of bug for good?
options: `await saveOrder(order)`, and turn on `@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises` so lint flags every unawaited promise
steps.explain: Without `await`, the handler answers 201 before the save finishes, and a rejection is never seen by the `try`/`catch` around it. The lint rule finds every such call in the codebase, not just this one.

code: const err = new Error("Could not load prices", { cause: inner });
steps.explain: The outer message says what failed for the user; `cause` keeps the technical reason. Log both, and you can tell "the price service is down" from "our code has a bug" at a glance.

steps.prompt: The test suite takes 3 minutes and one test, "applies discount" in `src/cart.test.ts`, fails. What do you type to rerun only that test while you fix it?
steps.explain: A path fragment limits the files and `-t` the test names. Without `run`, vitest stays in watch mode and reruns that test on every save, which is exactly what you want while fixing it.

steps.prompt: Match each flag to what it does.
pairs: fails the run on any warning
runs the tests once and exits
runs only tests whose name matches
fails if any file is not formatted

steps.prompt: Checked by the JavaScript engine at run time, or only by the TypeScript compiler?
buckets: Compiler only, erased from the output

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: When you catch an error you cannot handle, rethrow it with `{ cause }` and a sentence about what you were doing. Run `eslint`, `prettier --check` and `vitest run` locally exactly as CI does, and keep `vitest` in watch mode with `-t` while you work on one test.
